content.introduction: The S&P 500 was upgraded by Citi, which reported that US equities reached new record highs driven by confirmation of a US-China trade deal, easing restrictions on rare earths, a ceasefire in the Israel-Iran conflict, and the removal of the Section 899 “retaliatory tax” from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The S&P 500 closed at 7,483.23, down 0.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite shed nearly 0.7% to close at 26,040.03. The upgrade by UBS raised its price target to $582 from $571, implying 14% upside from Tuesday’s close.
body:
The S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq surged by 3.44%, 3.82%, and 4.25%, respectively. US equities reached new record highs driven by confirmation of a US-China trade deal, easing restrictions on rare earths, a ceasefire in the Israel-Iran conflict, and the removal of the Section 899 “retaliatory tax” from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). [...] US equities reached new record highs driven by confirmation of a US-China trade deal, easing restrictions on rare earths, a ceasefire in the Israel-Iran conflict, and the removal of the Section 899 “retaliatory tax” from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

### The Fed Is Divided Over the Timing of Rate Cuts [...] We would expect that if tariff inflation does not materialize during the summer, the Fed will recommence a cutting cycle no later than September, which will propel intermediate duration bond prices beyond this year’s gains.

But investor concerns over the new US budget bill’s impact on the fiscal deficit combined with increased Treasury issuance this fall after the debt ceiling is increased may prevent longer-term yields from moving significantly lower absent a marked economic slowdown.

The bank upgraded the stock to buy from neutral. It also raised its price target to $582 from $571, implying 14% upside from Tuesday's close.

"Investors might be reluctant to buy the dip on defense because of top-down concerns regarding 'Peak Defense' and a possible 'Blue Wave'," analyst John Godyn said Wednesday in a note to clients. "We believe LMT is a good example of a defense stock that historically bounces back consistently and sharply after moves lower." [...] The moves come after the major averages closed out a strong start to 2026. In the first six months of the year, the Dow climbed 8.9%, marking its best first-half performance since 2021. The broad market S&P 500 rose 9.6%, and the Nasdaq climbed 12.8%. The small-cap Russell 2000 surged nearly 22% to clinch its best first-half performance since 1991. [...] The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed marginally lower, down almost 14 points, to finish the day at 52,305.24. However, it sailed to a new intraday record of 52,742.66 earlier in the session.

The S&P 500 finished down 0.2% to end the day at 7,483.23. The Nasdaq Composite shed nearly 0.7% to close at 26,040.03.

— Liz Napolitano

The reusability of SpaceX's new super-heavy rocket is the linchpin of the technology conglomerate's future success, according to Wedbush analyst Dan Ives.
